title: Investigate & Fix: Customer prompt/eval quality regression after serving sampling/stop-token defaults
creator: Asha Kapoor
description:
Summary: Multiple customers reported sudden drops in prompt/eval pass rates after an internal serving change that adjusted sampling defaults and stop-token handling. Regressions observed across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments but with different failure modes: Hosted customers saw unexpected trailing tokens and hallucinations; Dedicated pools reported increased token truncation mid-answer; Private customers reported that configured stop tokens were ignored in some rollout shards.

Scope & Impact:
- Affected customers: three enterprise customers escalated (Acme Retail, FinEdge, Voyager Health) plus multiple PLG accounts showing degraded eval results.
- User-facing impact: evaluation suites show a 12-35% relative drop in prompt match rates for affected prompts; production customer features returned malformed or incomplete responses.
- Surface: generation endpoints (chat & text completion) across hosted API and Dedicated; Private deployments show inconsistent behavior depending on control-plane version.

Repro steps:
1) Send canonical prompt used in customer's eval harness with prior baseline config (temperature=0.0, top_p=1.0, stop_tokens=["\n\n"]).
2) Compare output with cluster that received the new serving defaults (temperature defaulted to 0.7 in some runtimes, stop token trimming applied earlier).
3) Observe: outputs contain extra continuing text (sampling noise) or are truncated right before expected finalization tokens.

Root cause hypothesis: During the runtime-1.22 rollout we changed global sampling defaults and added an early stop-token trimming optimization to speed up batch tokenization. The combination caused two interactions: 
- For deterministic prompts previously relying on temperature=0.0, the implicit temperature change introduced stochasticity, breaking exact-match evals.
- Stop-token trimming moved to a pre-generation stage in some execution paths, which caused tokenization/sequence boundary mismatches when stop tokens included multi-byte or whitespace-prefixed sequences.
- Routing differences across Hosted/Dedicated/Private meant some customer traffic still on older kernel selections, causing inconsistent behavior across fleets.

Temporary mitigations applied:
- Rolled back global sampling defaults on Hosted by flipping runtime flag runtime/sampling/policy=legacy for affected customers (rolled back 2026-03-05 03:20 UTC).
- Provided customer-scoped override docs and support snippet: set sampling: {temperature:0, top_p:1.0} and explicit stop_token trimming client-side.
- Opened emergency hotfix branch and gated the stop-token trimming optimization behind a per-customer opt-in flag.

Work already done and artifacts:
- Investigation notes: Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/stop-token-sampling-regression (internal doc)
- Repro harness and test vectors: https://github.com/redwood/repro-harness/pull/86 (vectors + CI job)
- Hotfix PR (gated opt-out for stop-trim): https://github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/4321 (in review)
- Rollback PR for sampling defaults: https://github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/4330 (merged 2026-03-05)
acceptance_criteria: All affected customers back to baseline eval pass rates (<=3% relative delta) verified by customer-run evals or by our reproducible harness
Stop-token handling restored to pre-change semantics for default rollout, with optimization behind an opt-in flag
Runtime tests added: tokenization/stop-token boundary unit tests and end-to-end evals for deterministic prompts
Config gating in Console to allow per-customer sampling/stop-token overrides
Postmortem published and communicated to affected customers with timeline and remediation guidance
